input: Assess the credit and counterparty risk of Wolfspeed

debt_events.summary: Filed a prepackaged Chapter 11 case (S.D. Texas). The plan cut total debt by about 70% (about $4.6B) and annual cash interest by about 60%. This is a default and distressed restructuring within the last 18 months.

Emerged from Chapter 11 and adopted fresh-start accounting. Issued $1.3B of New Senior Secured Notes due 2030, plus 2L PIK toggle notes and 2L convertible notes (Renesas and non-Renesas) due 2031. Maturities were extended to 2030 and later.

Issued $379.0M of 3.5% 1.5-lien convertible senior secured notes due 2031 and raised about $96.9M from a stock and pre-funded warrant private placement. The proceeds repurchased $475.9M principal of the New Senior Secured Notes for $524.3M, including make-whole and accrued interest.
The New Senior Secured Notes did not meet the interest-rate step-down condition, so the 15.875% cash rate stays in place on the $635.9M outstanding.
Company reports compliance with all debt covenants, including the $350M minimum liquidity covenant. No current maturities; the earliest maturity is the senior secured notes due 2030-06-23.

Announced a conditional commitment from the Department of War Office of Strategic Capital for a senior secured delayed-draw term loan of up to $1.5B over 30 years. It is not signed or funded. Conditions include due diligence, definitive agreements, appropriations, and amendments or waivers to existing debt. Warrants for up to 7.5% of fully diluted equity would be issued as tranches fund. The company says there is no assurance the loan will close.

distress_signals.summary: Gross margins remain negative: GAAP -22% and non-GAAP -13% in Q1 FY2027. Adjusted EBITDA was -$54.7M and free cash flow -$96.5M. Revenue fell about 21% year on year to $155.0M. Cash plus investments fell about $93M in the quarter.
Further headcount reductions in Q2 FY2026, Q4 FY2026 and Q1 FY2027, mostly severance. Q1 FY2027 restructuring and other expenses were $14.3M, including $4.0M of idle-facility costs.

The FY2026 10-K reports the closure of the 150mm Durham, NC device fab, consolidating power device production at the Mohawk Valley 200mm fab. Headcount was 2,371 at 2026-06-28. Two customers made up 38% of post-emergence revenue.
China accounted for 32.9% of Q1 FY2027 revenue. The securities class action (Zagami v. Wolfspeed) was dismissed without prejudice on 2026-08-12, but plaintiffs appealed on 2026-09-11.
CFO turnover: CFO Neill Reynolds left in May 2025 and Kevin Speirits served as interim CFO. Gregor van Issum was appointed CFO effective 2025-09-01. No CFO change since then.
No going-concern language. Management says liquidity is sufficient for at least 12 months. The auditor is PwC (since 2013); no auditor change.

ownership.value: Public (NYSE: WOLF) after Chapter 11. Former convertible noteholders and Renesas hold significant stakes. Renesas received 16,852,372 common shares on 2026-01-29 after CFIUS clearance and took one board seat (Aris Bolisay). It also holds $203.6M of 2L convertible notes and a warrant for 4,943,555 shares. Secondary reports put Renesas at roughly 37% of shares outstanding; the filings I read do not confirm a percentage.

output.risk_rationale: Wolfspeed went through a prepackaged Chapter 11 from June to September 2025, and it still loses money: Q1 FY2027 adjusted EBITDA was -$54.7M, free cash flow was -$96.5M, and its $635.9M of senior secured notes carry a 15.875% cash coupon. Against that, it has $995.1M of cash and investments, no maturities before 2030, total debt principal of about $1.77B, covenant compliance, and no going-concern language. At the current burn rate, cash would fall to the $350M minimum liquidity covenant in roughly 6-7 quarters. That makes the conditional, unfunded $1.5B Office of Strategic Capital loan and the promised margin recovery key; if either fails, the call should move to high.
